title: Flank & Queen's Indian Set-ups
intro: Meet 1...c5 with 2.c3 to keep a strong centre, and answer 1...Nf6 2.Nf3 e6 with Bf4, e3 and Nbd2.
variation: d2d4 c7c5, d2d4 g8f6 g1f3 c7c5, d2d4 g8f6 g1f3 e7e6 c1f4 b7b6

lessons.title: Meeting 1...c5
lessons.summary: Hold d4 with 2.c3 instead of entering sharp Benoni lines.

steps.text: Some players try to pull you out of the London on move one with 1...c5.

steps.hint: Push the queen's pawn two squares.

steps.text: Black strikes at d4 at once with 1...c5.
Keep a pawn in the centre instead of pushing to d5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 2.c3 to keep a stable London structure.
steps.ifRight: If Black takes on d4, cxd4 leaves you with a healthy centre.

feedback.d4d5: 2.d5 enters sharp Benoni lines. 2.c3 keeps the game in calm London territory.

steps.text: Black develops with 2...Nf6 to stop e4.
Here Black traded early with 2...cxd4. Recapture and keep the centre.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3.cxd4 to build a strong centre and open the c-file.
steps.ifRight: You can follow with Nf3, Bf4 and Nc3.

lessons.title: Meeting 1...Nf6 2.Nf3 c5
lessons.summary: Meet 2...c5 with 3.c3 and follow with Bf4.

steps.text: Black can also challenge d4 on move two with 2...c5.
Support d4 calmly with the c-pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3.c3 to keep a firm pawn on d4.
steps.ifRight: Now Bf4 and e3 follow naturally.

feedback.d4d5: 3.d5 leads to Benoni theory. 3.c3 stays in London structures.

steps.text: Black plays 3...e6 to free the dark-squared bishop.
Bring your dark-squared bishop out before playing e3.
steps.ifRight: Next come e3, Nbd2 and Bd3.

steps.text: What if Black takes on d4 right after 3.c3?
Recapture on d4 to hold the centre.
steps.ifRight: White follows with Nc3, Bf4 and e3.

lessons.title: Meeting ...e6 and ...b6
lessons.summary: Guard e4 with Nbd2 and keep h3 ready for your bishop.

steps.text: Against 1...Nf6 2.Nf3 e6 3.Bf4, Black often fianchettoes on the queenside with 3...b6.
Open the path for your light-squared bishop and support d4.
steps.ifRight: White builds a calm structure against the b7 bishop.

steps.text: Black puts the bishop on the long diagonal with 4...Bb7.
Develop your queen's knight and reinforce e4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.Nbd2 so you can play Bd3, c3 and castle.
steps.ifRight: Notice how Nbd2, Bd3 and Nf3 keep e4 well guarded.

steps.text: Black develops with 5...Be7, preparing to castle or jump with ...Nh5.
Give your bishop a retreat square on h2 before castling.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.h3 so ...Nh5 never wins your bishop pair.
steps.ifRight: Next come Bd3, c3 and O-O, with a rock-solid position.

feedback.f1d3: 6.Bd3 is playable, though 6...Nh5 forces you to give up the bishop pair or play Bg5.
